fair_value_reason: The round-2 forecasters' mean ($355.6; range $353-359), rounded. My check: NTM EPS at Sep 2027 of ~$19.7-19.8 x 18x = ~$355, and NTM FCF of ~$5.1-5.3B at a 5.25-5.5% yield on ~270M shares = ~$350-360, less $0-1 of expected receivable write-down. No agent has a share-count or EPS-base error. Excludes ~$6.4 of dividends.
supervisor_summary: Round 2 converged tightly: fair values of $353-359 (mean $356), P(close >= $332 in 12 months) of 0.55-0.60, and every agent now uses the same corrected facts: Q3 on Oct 30, the CR to Dec 11, Block VI already awarded, the $1.3B tracked-vehicle receivable and the Oct 9 ex-dividend. I verified the new round-2 evidence (GAMA deliveries, EB hiring, the 10-Q Combat detail, the defense-prime drawdown base rate) and corrected two minor slips, none of which moves a number. So I keep the mean ladder, $356 fair value and a $275 thesis break, at low confidence. The trade is a modest ~+4% median price gain plus ~1.9% dividend, driven by the defense multiple through the midterms and budget and by the January 2027 guide.
key_drivers: 2027 EPS vs the $18.59 consensus (range $17.59-19.35); first FY27 guide and Gulfstream production 'clarity' in late January 2027.

Defense multiple (~18x NTM): set by the Nov 3 midterms, the Dec 11 CR expiry and a reconciliation that Senate appropriators ruled out in June. LMT and NOC are down 23-33% from February highs, so this is a sector de-rating, not GD-specific.
Gulfstream: H1 deliveries 79 vs 74 (GAMA), 1.5x book-to-bill and tight used large-cabin inventory, against the G280 run-out in Q2 2027 before G300 EIS in late 2027/early 2028.
Marine execution on the $76.6B July award: EB is hiring 8,000 in 2026 (4,000+ by July) and margins are 7.3-7.4%. EB EAC charges are the main idiosyncratic left tail.

Combat: munitions and European vehicles (+$331M H1) outrun the U.S. vehicle decline (-$217M, M10 Booker ended), and the $1.3B tracked-vehicle receivable has not paid down. Watch it at the Oct 30 print.
